Risk call on MINDS: this is a buy-side refusal, not a sized trade.

Refuse at any size. The curve shows bundle_share 0.8355, meaning most early supply was bundled, and the first two minutes after graduation had a sell-to-buy ratio of 1.09 with a launch bot present. The coin is 47% off its 30-minute high with a -45% 30-minute return, and sellers (259) are rising alongside buyers in the last 15 minutes. Pool depth of 63 SOL is thin for a $20 ticket once fees and impact take 1.4-5.1%.

If the desk overrode this, the ceiling would be $5, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold, but I would not recommend it. Skip.
memos.scout:
Honest case for buying MINDS now: limited, and it rests on a few numbers.

- Organic class, no airdrop dump seen, and the coin is still alive at 30.6 min.
- Broad early participation: 998 curve buyers, 420 buyers in the first two minutes after graduation (excluding us), top-5 buyer share only 11.9%, top-3 holder share 8.1%.
- Last 15 minutes showed net positive flow (+10.24 SOL) and a +22% return, with 370 buyers against 259 sellers.

The case against is stronger. The coin is down 47% from its 30-minute high, and the 30-minute return is -45%. Sell-to-buy ratio in the launch window was about 1.09, and the 15-minute window still shows sellers taking out 167.7 SOL. The 83.6% bundle share on the curve signals coordinated early buying, and a launch bot was present. Pool depth is only 63 SOL, so round-trip costs of 1.4-5.1% are likely at the high end. A +22% bounce after a 47% drawdown is as consistent with a dead-cat bounce as with renewed demand.

Verdict: the brief does not show that demand will hold for the next 30-60 minutes. The positives are real but thin, and they are outweighed by the drawdown, heavy sell pressure, and bundling. I'd pass.
memos.skeptic: Most likely loss: a rug or insider distribution by the bundle group. The curve shows bundle_share 0.8355, meaning roughly 84% of curve activity came from bundled wallets, and the classification is labeled ORGANIC, which doesn't match that concentration. The first two minutes after graduation had a launch bot present and a sell-to-buy ratio of 1.09, so early sellers already matched buyers. Price is down 47% from its 30-minute high with a -45% 30-minute return, and the last 15 minutes show net outflow of 10.24 SOL against 167.74 SOL sold. A $20 entry on a 63 SOL pool also faces 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs. The bundled supply can dump into thin depth, so I'd skip.
